# dsh-workspace-launcher — v2.0.0 for DeepSeek Harness 0.2.x
Open the current session's workspace directory in **File Explorer**, **VS Code**, or a **terminal**,
or copy its path, straight from the **Session header**.
> 中文文档见 README.zh.md。

| Plugin | `dsh-workspace-launcher` 2.0.0 |
| Harness | DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.2** (Desktop or

`dsh web`) |

## What changed from 0.1.x
0.1.x patched `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace`'s compiled bundle to inject five rows into the
workspace “...” menu, then registered a plugin. DSH 0.2 builds client packages as dynamic bundles, s
o editing an installed bundle is unsafe and unsupported.
2.0 keeps the same host route and moves the UI to the documented slot API:

| Patched `dsh-client-ui-workspace` bundle | No patches at all |
| Rows in the Workspace “...” menu
| **The same menu**, with the four rows appended to the shipped Rename/Delete menu; plus a Session-h

eader menu |
| Workspace path came from the patched row | `cwd` from `useSessions`, workspace `path`

as fallback |
| Toasts injected into `document.body` | Status line inside the plugin's own popover

as fallback |
| Toasts injected into `document.body` | Status line inside the plugin's own popover |
DSH 0.2 has no workspace-menu slot (only session row menus are extendable). The plugin therefore rem
embers the workspace whose “...” button was pressed (its `aria-label` carries the title), watches fo
r the shipped menu to appear, and appends the four rows inside that menu. The built-in Rename/Delete
rows and their behavior are untouched.
DSH 0.2 also ships a built-in **Open In…** split button (`dsh-client-ui-open-in-app`) that opens the
session directory in any installed application from the application catalog. This plugin stays comp
lementary: it guarantees Explorer, VS Code, a terminal, and a clipboard copy even when the catalog p
ntees Explorer, VS Code, a terminal, and a clipboard copy even when the catalog probe finds nothing.
## What it does
The Session header gains an **Open workspace** button, and a **right-click on a workspace row** in t
he sidebar opens the same menu:

- **Open in File Explorer** — `explorer.exe` via `cmd /c start`, Finder, or `xdg-open`.
- **Open in

VS Code** — `code`, with Windows registry/`App Paths`/standard-path fallbacks.
- **Open in terminal*
* — Windows Terminal (`wt.exe`), falling back to a visible PowerShell window; Terminal.app or `x-ter

minal-emulator` elsewhere.
- **Copy workspace path** — clipboard, with a `document.execCommand` fall

-emulator` elsewhere.
- **Copy workspace path** — clipboard, with a `document.execCommand` fallback.
The host half exposes `POST /workspace-open/open` with `{ path, app }`. It validates that the path i
s absolute, strips trailing separators (Windows quoting), spawns detached with stdio ignored, and ne
ver blocks the harness. Failures are returned as JSON and shown in the popover.

Install this folder as a bundle and enable `dsh-workspace-launcher`. The bundle lives in `plugin/dsh
-workspace-launcher/`.

If you used the 0.1.x installer, **restore the original** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace` pac

## Verify

1. Open a session whose workspace directory exists.
2. The Session header shows **Open workspace**;

hover it — the tooltip is the resolved directory.
3. Click → four menu rows. Each launches the expec

ted application.
4. “Copy workspace path” copies the directory; the popover shows `Path copied`.
5.
A session without a directory shows `This session has no workspace path`.
## Uninstall
Disable/remove the bundle and reload. Nothing else was modified.
